chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Regarding the barren land which a man holds as a mortgage, wherein there is no fruit, so he cultivates it and spends his wealth upon it, it is reckoned for him his expenditure and his work exclusively. Then he considers the share of the land, so he reckons it from the wealth with which the land was mortgaged until his wealth is fulfilled. So when his wealth is fulfilled, let him hand over the land to its owner.'

key_terms.يَرْتَهِنُهَا: He holds it as a mortgage/security deposit

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a debtor who cultivates mortgaged barren land to repay a debt?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni, clarifies the distribution of value in a mortgage of barren land (al-baww), prioritizing the recovery of the creditor's principal debt after deducting the debtor's exclusive expenses and labor. It establishes a fair economic mechanism where the creditor's claim is limited to the secured amount, preventing unjust enrichment from the land's appreciation or the debtor's cultivation efforts. This principle underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on equity in financial transactions, ensuring that the debtor retains the benefit of their labor while the creditor recovers their exact stake.
